raw_signature: cannot read propert(?:y|ies) of undefined(?: \(reading ['"]?([^'")\s]+)['"]?\))?|cannot read property ['"]?([^'"\s]+)['"]? of undefined
plain_translation: You told the game to use {value}, but it has not been created yet. The name is either spelled differently or it does not exist at this point.
checklist_fixes: Check the variable named in the error , it is undefined . Add a console.log() just before the crash line to see its value.

If accessing a DOM element, make sure the HTML element exists and your script runs after the page loads: put your <script> at the end of <body> or use document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', ...) .
If reading from an array, check the index is not out of range: arr[5] is undefined if the array has fewer than 6 items.
Add a guard before using the value: if (player) { player.score += 1; }
problem_html: The console shows TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'x') or Cannot read property 'x' of undefined. Your code tried to access a property on something that doesn't exist yet.
prevention_html: Use optional chaining: player?.score returns undefined instead of crashing. Always initialise variables before using them: let player = null; then check before using.
keywords: cannot read properties of undefined reading TypeError undefined is not a function null property access uncaught typeerror

plain_translation: JavaScript cannot find that name. It may be misspelled, in another scope, or never declared.
checklist_fixes: Check spelling , Score and score are different in JavaScript.
Make sure you declared the variable with let , const , or var before using it.
Check the variable is declared in the right scope , variables declared inside a function can't be used outside it.
If the variable should be global, declare it at the top of the file, not inside a function.
problem_html: The console shows ReferenceError: score is not defined (or similar). JavaScript can't find the variable you're using.
prevention_html: Always declare variables at the top of the block where they're needed. Use const for things that don't change, let for things that do. A linter (like ESLint) catches these errors before you run the code.
keywords: referenceerror is not defined variable not declared let const var typo name undefined variable

plain_translation: The drawing code is running, but it is drawing to the wrong place or before the canvas is ready.
checklist_fixes: Check you called canvas.getContext('2d') and saved the result.
Make sure the canvas has width/height attributes (not just CSS size).
Drawing coordinates start at top-left (0,0). Check your x/y values.
If using requestAnimationFrame , make sure the function actually calls itself.
problem_html: Your <canvas> element is on the page but nothing appears on it. The drawing code runs but the canvas stays blank.
prevention_html: Set canvas width/height in JavaScript, not CSS: canvas.width = 800. CSS size scales the visual but not the buffer.
keywords: canvas not drawing rendering blank context2d

plain_translation: The element is not there when the listener is added, or another element is catching the click.
checklist_fixes: Make sure the element exists in the DOM when you add the listener , check for null.
Event names are case-sensitive: "click" not "Click" .
Check if another element with a higher z-index is blocking clicks (pointer-events).
For keydown, the target must have focus or you need to listen on document .
problem_html: You add an event listener for click or keydown but the callback never runs. The element exists but doesn't respond.
prevention_html: Put your script at the end of <body> or use DOMContentLoaded. Log the element to console before adding listeners.
keywords: event not firing click keydown listener addEventListener

plain_translation: The image path is wrong, or the drawing happens before the image has loaded.
checklist_fixes: Check the image path , use relative paths from the HTML file, not absolute.
Wait for onload before drawing: img.onload = function() { ... }
For local files, use a local server (VS Code Live Server, Python http.server).
CORS: cross-origin images may load but can't be drawn to canvas without the server allowing it.
problem_html: An image shows as a broken link or doesn't appear. The onload callback may never fire.
prevention_html: Always use img.onload , never draw immediately after setting src. Use a local server for development.
keywords: image not loading broken src cross origin cors

plain_translation: The mixer needs a click, a supported file, or a different format before it will play.
checklist_fixes: Browsers block autoplay until a user interacts. Play audio inside a click/keydown handler.
Call audio.play() and catch the promise: audio.play().catch(e => ...)
Check the audio file path and format (MP3/WAV/OGG supported by most browsers).
Make sure the Audio object isn't muted and volume isn't 0.
problem_html: Audio plays silently or not at all. The Audio element loads but .play() returns a rejected promise.
prevention_html: Use the Web Audio API or play sound on user's first click. "Click to start" screens solve the autoplay policy problem.
keywords: sound not playing audio autoplay policy browser silent
